submissions.title: San Francisco Mayor Signs 45-Day Data Center Moratorium
submissions.excerpt: Mayor Daniel Lurie on Friday signed the moratorium, which lasts 45 days
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: San Francisco enacted a 45-day pause on new data-center approvals, covering expansions of existing facilities as well as new builds, while the Planning Department studies impacts; it can extend up to 22 months if a significant environmental impact is found. No tracked SF-area project in the current snapshot, but this is a notable new restriction given SF's status as an AI hub. submissions.title: Duke Energy Reaches Settlement on Large-Load Tariff for Data Centers in North Carolina
submissions.excerpt: large-load customers of 50 MW or more with an 80% load factor that sign an electric service agreement after June 1, 2026
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Duke Energy's two NC utilities, the NC Public Staff, and (per reporting) Amazon, Google, Meta and Microsoft agreed to a large-load tariff for data centers: a separate High Load Factor rate schedule, minimum monthly bills near 75% of projected demand, and upfront/deposit requirements for dedicated facilities and shared grid upgrades. Still needs NC Utilities Commission approval, reportedly expected around mid-November 2026. Possibly relevant to the tracked North Carolina project 'AWS Richmond County' (UNDER_CONSTRUCTION) since Duke Energy Progress serves that region -- a human should confirm the utility match before linking, since this could not be verified against the live tracker (see caveat below). submissions.title: Lexington Council Extends Data Center Moratorium to October 2027
submissions.excerpt: Council members voted unanimously to extend a moratorium on new data center development until Oct. 2027
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Lexington, KY extended its data-center moratorium (first passed June 2026, previously set to expire Oct. 31, 2026) to October 2027, and separately passed a zoning text amendment: bans facilities over 50,000 sq ft, caps energy use at 25 MW, adds noise limits, and restricts smaller facilities to industrial zones. Note: one earlier (July 2026) report cited a 40,000 sq ft cap instead of 50,000 -- the October reports consistently say 50,000, but the final adopted ordinance text should be checked. No tracked Lexington project in the current snapshot; flagging as a new-market restriction precedent. submissions.title: Memphis Council Delays Vote on Proposed Data Center Moratorium Amid Protests
submissions.excerpt: The Memphis City Council postponed its planned final vote on Ordinance 5982, a 12-month data center moratorium, to October 20, 2026
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION (pending, not yet decided): Memphis City Council has twice postponed a final vote on Ordinance 5982, a proposed 12-month moratorium on new data-center approvals; the vote is now scheduled for October 20, 2026 -- two days after this submission. Council has said it would not apply to xAI's existing sites but would pause approval of new ones pending a zoning review. Directly relevant to the tracked, UNDER_CONSTRUCTION project 'xAI Colossus 2' (Memphis, TN) -- flagging ahead of the vote since the outcome is unknown; recommend a human follow up after Oct 20 to log the actual result.
